title: Pulling back from the point
statement:
Let $*_{\mathrm{proét}}$ be the pro-étale site of a point: profinite sets with
the coherent topology ([det-def-sfb-condensed-ring]). For a scheme $X$ let
$X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ be its small pro-étale site ([def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]),
and let $\pi_X\colon X\to\Spec\Z$ be the structure morphism. Since $\Spec\Z$ is
terminal, $\pi_Y\circ f=\pi_X$ for every morphism $f\colon X\to Y$.

1. **Profinite sets as pro-étale schemes.** For a profinite set $S$, let
   $LC(S,\Z)$ be the ring of locally constant functions $S\to\Z$. If $S_i$ runs
   over the finite quotients of $S$, then
   $$
   \Spec LC(S,\Z)=\lim_i\coprod_{S_i}\Spec\Z .
   $$
   The morphism $\Spec LC(S,\Z)\to\Spec\Z$ is weakly étale. Precomposition
   makes $S\mapsto\Spec LC(S,\Z)$ a functor
   $$
   u\colon *_{\mathrm{proét}}\longrightarrow(\Spec\Z)_{\mathrm{proét}} .
   $$
   It preserves finite limits, it sends finite jointly surjective families to
   pro-étale coverings, and it is continuous.

2. **Test objects.** For a scheme $X$ and a profinite set $S$, put
   $$
   X[S]:=\Spec LC(S,\Z)\times_{\Spec\Z}X=\lim_i\coprod_{S_i}X .
   $$
   The functor $u_X\colon *_{\mathrm{proét}}\to X_{\mathrm{proét}}$,
   $S\mapsto X[S]$, is $u$ followed by base change along $\pi_X$.

3. **Inverse image from the point.** Let
   $p_*\colon\Sh((\Spec\Z)_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)\to\Sh(*_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$,
   $(p_*G)(S)=G(\Spec LC(S,\Z))$, be restriction along $u$. Define
   $$
   p^*:=\mathrm{sheafify}\circ\operatorname{Lan}_{u^{\mathrm{op}}}\colon
   \Sh(*_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)\longrightarrow\Sh((\Spec\Z)_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab).
   $$
   Then $p^*$ is left adjoint to $p_*$. For the tensor products of
   [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-tensor-closed], $p^*$ is strong monoidal and braided.

4. **Inverse image to $X$.** Define
   $$
   p_X^*:=\pi_X^*\circ p^*\colon
   \Sh(*_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)\longrightarrow\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab),
   $$
   where $\pi_X^*$ is the pullback of [def-sfb-finite-upper-star]
   for $\mathcal A=\Ab$. It is strong monoidal and braided, since $p^*$ and
   $\pi_X^*$ are ([def-sfb-finite-upper-star-monoidal],
   [lem-sfb-finite-upper-star-braided]). It is a left
   adjoint, with right adjoint $G\mapsto\bigl(S\mapsto G(X[S])\bigr)$; so
   $p_X^*$ is the inverse image along $u_X$.

proof.text: The structure maps satisfy $\pi_Y\circ f=\pi_X$, since $\Spec\Z$ is terminal ([lem-weil-pbc-spec-z-terminal]): both are the unique morphism $X\to\Spec\Z$. For $u$, use [def-sfb-profinite-to-proetale]: its map on $g:S'\to S$ is induced by $h\mapsto h\circ g$. Identity and composition follow from precomposition and the contravariance of $\Spec$. The weakly étale assertion is [lem-sfb-lc-weakly-etale]. Preservation of finite limits, finite jointly surjective covers, and sheaves under restriction are respectively [lem-sfb-profinite-to-proetale-finite-limits], [lem-sfb-profinite-to-proetale-cover-preserving], and [lem-sfb-profinite-to-proetale-continuous].

Use [def-sfb-profinite-test-objects] for $u_X$ and its formula $X[S]=\lim_i\coprod_{S_i}X$. At $X=\Spec\Z$, the canonical identification $\Spec LC(S,\Z)\times_{\Spec\Z}\Spec\Z\cong\Spec LC(S,\Z)$ identifies its finite-quotient diagram with $\coprod_{S_i}\Spec\Z$. Thus the same formula also gives the inverse-limit identity in part 1. These identities mean the canonical isomorphisms of schemes, compatible with maps of finite quotients.

source.place: parts 1 and 2; second paragraph, including the absolute specialization

proof.text: Take $p_*$ to be restriction, as in [def-sfb-point-lower-star]. By [lem-sfb-point-lan-exists], the underlying abelian presheaf of every condensed abelian group has the required left Kan extension. Hence [def-sfb-point-upper-star] constructs the stated functor by that Kan extension followed by sheafification. The natural bijections $\Hom(p^*F,G)\cong\Hom(F,p_*G)$ are [def-sfb-point-adjunction].

source.place: part 3; third paragraph, construction and adjunction

proof.text: For the sheafified objectwise tensor product over $\Z$, [lem-sfb-point-upper-star-unit] supplies the lax structure on $p_*$, the adjoint oplax structure on $p^*$ and its invertible unit comparison. [lem-sfb-point-upper-star-tensor] supplies its invertible tensor comparisons. [lem-sfb-point-upper-star-braided] states that these give a strong monoidal functor compatible with symmetry. These three nodes use the tensor product of [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor] for $\mathcal A=\Ab$; it is the one of [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-tensor-closed] in the item: both are sheafifications of the objectwise abelian-group tensor product, with sheafified constant unit $\Z$.

source.place: part 3; third paragraph, monoidal and braided structures

proof.text:
Define $p_X^*=\pi_X^*\circ p^*$ using [def-sfb-upper-star-from-point], which also supplies its strong monoidal braided structure for the same sheaf tensor product. At $g=\pi_X$ and $\mathcal A=\Ab$, [def-sfb-finite-upper-lower-star-adjunction] and [def-sfb-point-adjunction] give, naturally in $F,G$,
$$\Hom(\pi_X^*p^*F,G)\cong\Hom(p^*F,\pi_{X*}G)\cong\Hom(F,p_*\pi_{X*}G).$$
This proves the claimed adjunction without any finiteness or properness assumption on $X$.

source.place: part 4; final paragraph, definition and composite adjunction

proof.text:
By [def-sfb-point-lower-star], [def-sfb-finite-lower-star] and [def-sfb-profinite-test-objects],
$$(p_*\pi_{X*}G)(S)=(\pi_{X*}G)(\Spec LC(S,\Z))=G(\Spec LC(S,\Z)\times_{\Spec\Z}X)=G(X[S]).$$
For $g:S'\to S$, both restriction maps are $G$ applied to the base change of the map induced by $h\mapsto h\circ g$; for a sheaf map $G\to H$, both maps at $S$ are its component at $X[S]$. Thus this is an identification of functors, natural in both variables. Its values are sheaves, since the composite direct image is sheaf-valued. The preceding adjunction therefore makes $p_X^*$ inverse image along $u_X$.
